executive_assessment.text: Local child-risk examples include Ferizaj/Prizren and Skenderaj/Mitrovica floods, while the Podujeva survey is indicative of respondents only.
Conflict-legacy ordnance constrained access to land/resources near Peja and Barë/Bajgora; clearance restored access, without quantifying climate-resilience gains.
Prizren water/land and gender priorities remain commitments whose implementation has not been verified.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024 reports: The brief names Ferizaj and Prizren as most vulnerable; children facing both hazard exposure and multidimensional poverty face greatest risks.
Source dated 2024 reports: After 2021 and 2023 were Kosovo's hottest years, family medicine centres in Pristina and Mitrovica reported more child admissions, especially above 30°C.

Source dated 2024 reports: Early-2023 floods affected about 22,000 people, including 3,000 children, mostly in Skenderaj and Mitrovica. Average-year floods affect about 10,000 people, damaging homes/schools and interrupting water and power.

Source dated 2024 reports: UNICEF flags disabled/health-condition and Roma, Ashkali and Egyptian children as facing added challenges; fires increased since 2007 in Mitrovica and Prizren, while human-caused fires removed 13% of Kosovo tree cover in 2001–2023.

Source dated 2023 reports: War ordnance contaminated wooded hills west of Peja, which faces flash floods, hotter summers and milder, less snowy winters. Clearance released 355,502 m², reopening park trails and resource access.

Source dated 2023 reports: In Mitrovica, war/industrial-closure migration and weakened services coexist with hotter summers, less snow and possible July–August drought. Clearance restored Barë grazing/firewood access and Bajgora woodland/pipeline access; wind power was exported.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: Prizren's 2023–2028 rural plan sets out 14 measures and 74 proposed actions with estimated costs of €22.4955 million across agriculture, biodiversity, forestry and rural tourism.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: The plan proposed irrigation-system rehabilitation studies, water-storage studies, Manastrica Dam design/construction for drinking water and irrigation, drip-irrigation subsidies and ponds for irrigation/firefighting; dam construction was scheduled for 2025–2028.

Source dated 2022-11 reports: The plan flags women in rural Prizren as potentially responsible for agricultural water management yet having limited water access; it calls for women's participation in planning, early warnings and drought-tolerant seed support.

Source dated 2026-08-05 reports: A June–July 2026 Podujeva survey of 101 respondents across 35 settlements found recurrent, materially damaging floods among participating households, with impacts concentrated on agricultural land and crops.
The non-representative Podujeva survey summary reports drinking-water interruptions, drainage/maintenance gaps and uneven warning access among respondents.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 17 of 18 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

The Kosovo NDC explicitly states a potential climate-to-conflict/social-tension risk concerning resource access; it does not document observed conflict attribution or establish a measured causal effect.
The 2018 strategy is dated and the full 2024 climate law text could not be accessed; current implementation capacity is not assessed here.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The Podujeva report PDF returned HTTP 429; findings are limited to the University of Prishtina/Municipality publisher record's explicit methods and results summary.
No directly inspected evidence established a climate-triggered violent-conflict event or a local climate-to-conflict causal estimate; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
Prizren plan actions and budgets are commitments, and several earlier milestones elapsed; implementation status was not checked.
GICHD's conflict-related land-access and resilience evidence is qualitative and report-period-specific; it does not quantify adaptation impacts.
